title: fix macOS 15 x86_64 GWT cache path and harden the seed sentinel
description:
### Intent

The cache-seed sentinel has been alerting on `os-cache-seed-e2e-macos-15-x86_64.yml` (#18359, #18373). Investigating #18373 turned up a transient DNS flake on top of a real, long-standing bug: **the macOS 15 x86_64 GWT cache has never once been saved.**

### The bug

`os-test-e2e-rstudio-desktop-os-macos-15-x86_64.yml` caches `package/osx/build-x86_64/gwt` (restore and save). But `package/osx/make-package:162` only suffixes the arm64 directory:

```sh
BUILD_DIR_X86_64="${PKG_DIR}/build"
BUILD_DIR_ARM64="${PKG_DIR}/build-arm64"
```

x86_64 builds into plain `package/osx/build`. The path looks copied from the arm64 workflow, where `build-arm64` is correct, and has been wrong since the workflow landed in #18324 — #18362 didn't touch it.

Every run of the seed shows the full cycle, even when it succeeds ([run 30313084528](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30313084528)):

- `Cache not found for input keys: rstudio-gwt-x86_64-PRETTY-v2-...`
- GWT compiles into `.../package/osx/build/gwt/bin`
- `Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist` → `Cache save failed.`

### Why it mattered

Because `rstudio-gwt-x86_64-` can never exist on main, the sentinel found it "evicted" on every 2-hourly cycle and dispatched another ~20-minute macOS build that again failed to save it. I confirmed `Evicted from main: rstudio-gwt-x86_64-` → `Dispatching` across four consecutive cycles; there were 12 dispatches on 2026-07-27 alone, on runners that bill at 10x. Repo cache usage sits at 9.79 GiB of the 10 GB quota, so the churn also pressured every other platform's caches. Separately, every macOS 15 x86_64 PR build paid the full GWT compile.

### Changes

1. **Path fix** — point the GWT restore/save at `package/osx/build/gwt`, with a comment recording why x86_64 differs from arm64. No key rotation needed; nothing was ever stored under the `-v2-` key.

2. **Sentinel hardening** (`os-cache-seed-sentinel.yml`) — #18373 was filed for a run that had already been superseded. The dispatch loop runs before the alert check, so the sentinel read a stale conclusion for a seed it had re-dispatched three seconds earlier:
   - Defer the alert while a newer run for that seed is `queued` or `in_progress`.
   - Close the alert issue once the seed's latest completed run succeeds, instead of only suppressing re-alerts while it stays open (both prior alerts needed closing by hand).

### Verification

- Both workflows parse as YAML; the sentinel's `run:` script passes `bash -n`.
- Drove the rewritten alert loop against a mock `gh` across all five branches — recovered-with-open-issue (closes), failure-with-retry-in-flight (defers), failure-with-nothing-in-flight (alerts), failure-with-issue-already-open (skips), and healthy (silent).
- The path fix needs a live seed run on main to confirm the save lands and `rstudio-gwt-x86_64-` appears in main's scope. Worth watching the first post-merge run.

### Note

Auto-closing is a slight behavior change: a genuinely flaky seed will now open and close issues repeatedly rather than holding one open. That seemed better than the current state, where every transient failure leaves manual cleanup, but happy to drop that half if you'd rather the alerts stay sticky.

Addresses #18373

title: e2e: match RStudio PIDs case-insensitively on macOS
description:
## Problem

Running the `@ai` e2e suite on macOS left an orphaned RStudio instance running after the run finished, showing "Posit Assistant not installed" in the chat pane.

`getRStudioPids()` ran `pgrep -x rstudio`, which is case-sensitive. The macOS executable is `/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/RStudio`, so the pattern never matched. The trailing `|| true` turned pgrep's no-match exit 1 into empty output, so the miss was silent — no warning, just an empty set.

`relaunchAfterRestart()` kills the post-restart instance by diffing RStudio PIDs before and after the restart. With both snapshots empty, it killed nothing and logged `New PIDs to kill: none`.

Nothing else caught the orphan. It is spawned by `ApplicationLaunch.launchRStudio` as a detached, `unref`'d process with no `--remote-debugging-port`, so the CDP port cleanup in `launchRStudioOnce`, the `process-reaper` backstop (which only tracks processes the fixture spawned), and `shutdownRStudio` (which only touches `session.rstudioProcess`) all miss it by design.

The orphan inherits the sandbox `RSTUDIO_CONFIG_ROOT` / `RSTUDIO_DATA_HOME` whose `pai` tree `uninstall-posit-ai.test.ts` had just deleted, which is why it renders the "not installed" state. That spec is the last `@ai` file to run under `workers: 1`, so the instance was left over at the end of every run.

Windows was unaffected (`Get-Process` is case-insensitive) and Linux was unaffected (`/usr/bin/rstudio` is already lowercase).

## Change

`pgrep -x rstudio` → `pgrep -ix rstudio`, with a comment recording why the `-i` matters.

## Testing

`npm run test:desktop -- --grep @ai` on macOS: all tests pass and no RStudio instance is left running afterward. `npm run typecheck` passes.

## Note

No NEWS.md entry — this changes e2e test infrastructure only, with no user-facing effect.

title: e2e: answer Posit Assistant AskUser prompts in chat guardrail tests
description:
Posit Assistant 0.7.8 can pause a turn on an `AskUser` question instead of acting. The question renders as a form (`Pending questions` tab strip, radio options, `Submit Answers`) and the turn stays active until it is answered, so `pollWithAllowDialogs` -- which waits for the stop button to disappear -- spun until the test timeout.

This showed up as `4: rename from project to outside is denied` in `chat-guardrails.test.ts` failing with a 120s timeout: asked to rename a file to a path outside the project, the assistant asked for confirmation rather than calling `file.rename()` and hitting the R guardrail.

Changes:

- `chat_pane.page.ts`: role-based locators for the question form (`pendingQuestions`, `submitAnswersBtn`) and an `isPendingQuestionVisible()` probe.
- `chat_pane.actions.ts`: `answerPendingQuestion()` selects a matching option and submits, waiting for the form to unmount. `pollWithAllowDialogs()` takes an optional `answerQuestion` matcher; without one, a pending question throws immediately with the question text instead of spinning to the timeout.
- `chat-guardrails.test.ts`: test 4 pins the prompt to R's `file.rename()` -- the assistant's own file tools and shell commands are not subject to `.rs.chat.withGuardrails`, so an unpinned prompt can move the file for real -- and answers affirmatively if asked, since declining would leave the file in place and pass the assertions without exercising the guardrail.

Test-only change; no NEWS entry.

Verification: `npm run typecheck` passes. These tests are gated on Posit AI credentials (`requireAiCredentials`), which CI does not provision, so they run locally only.

title: Add @chat tag for selecting the Posit Assistant e2e tests
description:
### Intent

The `@ai` tag selects both the Posit Assistant chat suites and the Copilot / Posit AI code-suggestion suites (ghost text, NES). There was no way to run just the Assistant tests. This adds a `@chat` tag for that.

```bash
npx playwright test --grep @chat
```

No associated GitHub issue -- this is test-tooling only.

### Approach

Every suite under `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/` is tagged `@chat`:

- The 17 suites that already carried `@ai` keep it and gain `@chat`, so `--grep @ai` selects exactly what it did before.
- `chat-guardrails-paths.test.ts` gets `@chat` only. It drives the guardrails through `.rs.chat.withGuardrails` from the R console with no AI provider in the loop, so it needs no credentials and must keep running under `--grep-invert @ai`. A note in its header docstring records that, so the missing `@ai` doesn't read as an oversight.

No change to `playwright.config.ts`: `@chat` is a selection tag, not an exclusion, so nothing goes into either project's `grepInvert`. No change to `tests/auth.setup.ts` either -- Playwright does not apply `--grep` to a project's dependencies, so the setup project still runs and provisions credentials under `--grep @chat`.

The CI workflows already forward a `grep` `workflow_dispatch` input to `--grep`, so `@chat` works there with no workflow changes.

`shiny-app-python.draft.ts` is left untagged: it is a `.draft.ts` wrapping a `describe.skip`, so it is never collected and a tag on it would be inert.

### Automated Tests

This change is entirely test metadata. Verified by test selection:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| `--grep @chat` | 80 tests / 19 files (78 plus the 2 setup tests) |
| chat files selected by `@chat` | 18 of 18 |
| `code_suggestions` + `edit_suggestions` under `@chat` | 0 |
| `--grep @ai` | 78 tests / 20 files, unchanged |
| `--grep-invert @ai` | still runs `chat-guardrails-paths.test.ts` (31 tests) |
| setup project under `--grep @chat` | both auth tests present |

### QA Notes

None. No product code is touched.

### Documentation

`e2e/rstudio/README.md`: a `@chat` row in the Available Tags table and a `--grep @chat` example in the Filtering by Tag section.

### Checklist

- [x] If this PR adds a new feature, or fixes a bug in a previously released version, it includes an entry in `NEWS.md` -- N/A, test tooling only, no user-facing change
- [x] If this PR adds or changes UI, the updated UI meets accessibility standards -- N/A, no UI change
- [ ] A reviewer is assigned to this PR
- [x] This PR passes all local unit tests

title: theme the Review Changes window (#9026)
description:
### Intent

Fixes #9026.

The Review Changes window (git/svn commit + history) always rendered light, however dark the editor theme was.

`VCSApplicationWindow` extends `SatelliteWindow`, which opts out of theming by default -- so the satellite's container never got the `rstudio-themes-*` classes and never had the editor theme CSS injected. (Satellites used to get the flat theme unconditionally; 490649125e moved that inside the `supportsThemes()` guard to fix #3153, which was *this window* rendering half dark. So opting back in means finishing the CSS this time.)

### Approach

- `VCSApplicationWindow.supportsThemes()` returns true, so the window gets the global theme classes (`rstudio-themes-dark` et al on an `rstudio_container`) and the editor theme stylesheet, and re-themes live when the theme changes.
- The changelist and the diff pane now follow the **editor** theme, exactly as the changelist does in the Git pane in the main window. The `whitebg` style that pinned them white is gone -- on the changelist it was actually clobbering the `ace_editor_theme` class `ChangelistTable` adds for itself, since UiBinder's `styleName` replaces rather than adds. The tables inside those panes now go transparent for *every* editor theme rather than only dark ones: the base stylesheet paints them a hard-coded white, which a light-but-not-white theme (Solarized Light, Dawn) would otherwise leave as a white slab inside a tinted pane.
- Diff rows tint the editor background with translucent overlays instead of fixed pastels, so insertions/deletions/context read correctly against any editor theme. The chunk/line action buttons (Stage chunk, Discard chunk) drop their sprite pills for flat translucent ones, keyed off `data-action` so Stage keeps its accent.
- The chrome -- toolbars, split panels, commit message box, Commit button, context selects, cell table headers, commit list selection, diff frame headers, commit TOC links -- gets dark styling from the same palette the theme-aware modal dialogs use. The panels and toolbars share one background so the commit area reads as a single surface, with the split draggers left as the seams.

The chrome follows the global theme and the changelist and diff follow the editor theme, which is how the Git pane behaves in the main window. (`global_theme` is `default` or `alternate`; a prefs file still holding the retired `classic` value is migrated to `default` the first time the Appearance pane is opened, and until then *any* window is half-themed -- `editor_dark` is applied but `rstudio-themes-dark` is not -- so this window is no exception to that pre-existing quirk.)

Also in this window, from hands-on review:

- header cells in the commit list carried the base style's light top and left borders, drawing a heavy outline around each one; they now match the changelist, and both tables inset their labels from the cell edge
- the history pager sat tight against the commit table above it
- the file list shows "No changes" when there is nothing to review, in place of an empty pane -- in the Review Changes window and in the Git and SVN panes, since they share the widget. Styled to match the Environment pane's "Environment is empty" message: centered, proportional at 90%, inheriting the theme foreground

### Verification

New e2e spec `e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/git/review_changes_theme.test.ts`: creates a git-backed project, applies Cobalt, opens the window, and asserts the theme classes reach the satellite container, the editor theme CSS is injected there, and both editor-themed panes paint dark; then switches back to a light theme and asserts the already-open window repaints light. Because those pane backgrounds come from the editor theme's own stylesheet, it also asserts two things only the new CSS can produce -- the cell tables inside the panes being transparent rather than white, and a chunk action pill being a flat translucent fill rather than a sprite -- so a dropped `@external` declaration cannot leave the spec green. Passes on desktop-dev.

Also inspected by hand on desktop-dev in Cobalt and Textmate (default), in both the Changes and the History view, with and without pending changes: toolbars, changelist, commit message box, diff, chunk buttons, commit list, commit detail, per-file diff frames and their "View file @ ..." links all read correctly, and the light appearance is unchanged apart from the header-cell tidy-up above.

SVN gets the parallel CSS changes but was not exercised at runtime.

title: make rsession long path aware on Windows
description:
Addresses #12806.

### Why R's own long path support never reached RStudio

R Core made R long-path aware in R 4.3.0, including `<longPathAware>true</longPathAware>` in the manifests for `Rterm.exe`, `Rgui.exe`, `Rscript.exe` and friends. But the manifest is a property of the *process*, and rsession loads `R.dll` into its own address space (`REmbeddedWin32.cpp`, plus `LIBR_LIBRARIES` linked into `rsession-shared`). R's front-end manifests therefore never apply under the IDE. R's [announcement](https://blog.r-project.org/2023/03/07/path-length-limit-on-windows/) calls this out: *"Applications embedding R must declare long-path awareness separately."* We hadn't.

So since R 4.3, R has supported long paths everywhere except inside RStudio.

### What's here

**Manifests.** `longPathAware` added to `rsession.exe`, `rsession-utf8.exe`, `consoleio.exe` and `diagnostics.exe`; `rpostback.exe` gains a manifest (and `.rc`) since it had none. All four existing manifests already declared the Windows 10 `supportedOS` GUID, which is the other precondition.

Note that Boost.Filesystem does not paper over `MAX_PATH` on its own — I checked its release history, and it never prepends `\\?\`. It calls the wide Win32 APIs directly, which means the whole of `FilePath` (`exists()`, `create_directories()`, `copy_file()`, …) inherits the process setting. That's why the manifest flip is the high-leverage change rather than a `\\?\` sweep.

**Buffer fixes the manifest newly exposes.**

| Site | Problem |
|---|---|
| `Win32System.cpp` `executablePath()` | `wchar_t[MAX_PATH]` with no truncation check — `GetModuleFileNameW` signals truncation by returning the buffer size, and only `== 0` was tested. Feeds `installPath()` and every derived resource path. Now grows and retries. |
| `Win32System.cpp` `ensureLongPath()`, `Win32FileMonitor.cpp` `ensureLongFilePath()` | `char[521]` + **ANSI** `GetLongPathName`, treating any non-zero return as success. On insufficient buffer that API returns the *required size* and writes nothing, so we built a `FilePath` from uninitialized stack. Both now go through a new `file_utils::longPathName()` using the two-pass wide pattern. The file monitor one also passed a UTF-8 string straight to an ANSI API. |
| `FilePath.cpp` `isWriteable()` | Probed with `GetTempFileNameW`, whose `lpPathName` is documented to fail above `MAX_PATH-14` (246 characters), so a deep directory reported as read-only. |
| 4x `SHGetFolderPathW` / `SHGetFolderPathAndSubDirW` | Contractually `MAX_PATH`-bound. Now `SHGetKnownFolderPath`, which allocates. This also fixes a leak in `userSettingsPath()`, which never called `CoTaskMemFree`. |
| 5x `PathFindOnPath` | Documented to take "a string of length MAX_PATH" and writes at most that regardless of the buffer given, so it cannot find programs under a long path. Replaced with `findProgramOnPath()`, which walks PATH and then the system directories. |

`SHGetKnownFolderPath` has no `A`/`W` pair — its out param is `PWSTR*`, so it's wide-only. Worth noting because this codebase never defines `UNICODE`, so every TCHAR-generic call (`GetModuleFileName`, `GetLongPathName`, `PathFindOnPath`, `ExpandEnvironmentStrings`, …) silently resolves to ANSI, and ANSI APIs cannot express long paths at all.

**Notebook path shortening.** The deepest path RStudio itself creates under a project was ~116 characters before the project path is even counted:

```
/.Rproj.user/shared/notebooks/<id8>-<stem>/1/<ctx16>/<chunk13>_t/<uuid32>.snapshot
```

The transient plot and snapshot leaf names are purely internal — they're renamed to their ordinal form (`000001.png`) when the chunk is committed, and nothing outside `NotebookPlots.cpp` matches on them. Shortening the snapshot id and the plot prefix takes 24 characters off the worst case with no compatibility cost and no cache version bump.

This matters because it's the failure users actually reported. [The second comment on the issue](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/12806#issuecomment-2981929334) describes a ~150-character project directory where notebook plotting failed: 150 + 116 > 260. At 150 + 92 it now fits, so that case is fixed *even on machines where long paths are not enabled*.

I deliberately stopped there. Getting another 8 characters would mean shortening the persisted `<ctx16>` directory, which requires bumping `kCacheVersion` and invalidating every user's chunk cache — not worth 8 characters.

### Explicitly out of scope

A project whose *own* directory exceeds `MAX_PATH`. Per the [`SetCurrentDirectory` docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setcurrentdirectory), *"Setting a current directory longer than MAX_PATH causes CreateProcessW to fail."* rsession sets its working directory to the project directory, so such a project would lose git, terminals, builds and `R CMD` entirely. That's an OS constraint, not something we can work around here; it's documented in a comment where the working directory is set, and in the NEWS entry. Files *below* a shorter project directory may now exceed `MAX_PATH` freely, which is the case that actually comes up.

### Tests

- `Win32SystemTests.cpp`: `executablePath()` resolves; `findProgramOnPath()` finds `cmd.exe`, returns empty for a missing program and for `""`, and handles an already-qualified path; `longPathName()` round-trips a short (8.3) name back to its long form and passes non-existent paths through unchanged.
- `FilePathTests.cpp`: a directory nested past 400 characters reports as writeable. This is the regression test for the `GetTempFileNameW` probe. It skips cleanly if the platform won't create a path that long (i.e. no `LongPathsEnabled`); our Windows CI sets that registry value already.

### Verification status

All cross-platform translation units compile locally. **The Windows-only code is not yet verified** — I developed this on macOS, so `Win32System.cpp`, `Win32User.cpp`, `Win32ChildProcess.cpp`, `Win32FileMonitor.cpp` and the `_WIN32` branches of `SessionGit.cpp` / `SessionSVN.cpp` have not been compiled, and nothing here has been run on Windows. Needs a Windows build plus manual confirmation that a >260-character path under a normal project now works with `LongPathsEnabled` set.

One thing I could not check: whether the shipped Electron `rstudio.exe` is long-path aware. Electron Forge only sets version metadata via `rcedit` (`forge.config.js`), not the manifest, and the Chromium `chrome.exe.manifest` revision I looked at does not set the flag. Worth a follow-up look, though rsession is what matters for R's file access.


---

### Corrections since first posting

- I originally claimed this PR also fixed a dangling pointer, `LPCWSTR folder = m_impl->Path.wstring().c_str()` binding to a destroyed temporary. **That was wrong.** Under `BOOST_FILESYSTEM_WINDOWS_API`, boost 1.91 `path::wstring()` returns `std::wstring const&` (`boost/filesystem/path.hpp:885`) -- a reference to the internal member -- so the pointer was valid. Rewriting `isWriteable()` is still correct for the `MAX_PATH` probe, but it was never a use-after-free. Thanks for catching it.
- `findProgramOnPath` no longer adds a new function: review pointed out that `Error findProgramOnPath(const std::string&, FilePath*)` already existed and was never `MAX_PATH`-bound. The system-directory fallback and PATH quote trimming were folded into it instead, so all callers share one search. Note this means the lookup no longer consults the current working directory the way `PathFindOnPath` did; `resolveCommand` already checks a CWD-relative name before reaching it.
- The two most important manifests were malformed: my comment prose contained `--`, which XML forbids inside a comment. `ManifestTests.cpp` now guards against that and against silently dropping `longPathAware`.

title: Harden Posit Assistant e2e tests to fail fast with attributable errors
description:
Four `@ai` chat tests turned any "assistant couldn't run the code" failure into an opaque 120s timeout (or a failure pointed at the wrong subsystem), because they waited for a success signal that never arrives when the assistant's `executeCode` tool is broken. This hardens each to fail fast with an attributable message. Diagnostic hardening only -- no product behavior change, no NEWS.md entry.

## Changes

- **`readline-notification.test.ts`** -- the poll only waited for the readline notification, so when the assistant never ran blocking code, R never blocked and the test hung to the 120s test timeout. Now detects the terminal "turn finished without blocking" state and fails with an attributable message. The poll is bounded below the per-test budget so this assertion reports the failure. Addresses #18365.

- **`shiny-app-r.test.ts`** -- the 300s completion poll ran under the 120s config default because the test body never set its own timeout, so slow Shiny cold-starts died before the poll's more informative timeout could fire. Sets a 360s test-body timeout that outlasts the poll, and fails fast when the turn finishes without the "app started" marker. Addresses #18366.

- **`plots-pane-activation.test.ts`** -- the assistant emits `PLOT_DONE_E2E` because the prompt tells it to, even when no plot was drawn, so a broken execution tool masqueraded as an #18037 regression. Now gates on real plot history (`clearPlots` enables only when the Plots pane has a plot) before the activation assertion. Addresses #18364.

- **`renameConversation` helper (`chat_pane.actions.ts`)** -- logged success right after pressing Enter, so a rename that never persisted surfaced downstream as an opaque `locator.click` timeout. Now asserts the renamed item is visible in the still-open history list before returning. Addresses #18363.

The "turn finished" fast-fail paths require the condition to hold across one short re-check, so a transient Stop-button gap between the assistant's intermediate tool steps does not produce a false failure.

## Notes

These are diagnostic-only. Against builds affected by posit-dev/assistant#1893 (the `r.getLogger is not a function` `executeCode` outage) and posit-dev/assistant#1894 (rename persistence), the tests will still fail -- they just pin the failure to the real cause instead of an opaque timeout.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` passes. The tests require AI credentials and a live Posit Assistant backend, so the runtime behavior needs manual verification against an `@ai` run.

title: Fix macOS e2e cache architecture collision and cold-build timeout
description:
Both macOS E2E engines shared a single R-library cache key (`runner.os`, which is just `macOS` for both). Because macOS 26 is arm64 and macOS 15 is x86_64, the x86_64 job restored the arm64 job's `pak`/`cli` binaries and couldn't load them ("incompatible architecture"), dying at the "Install e2e test dependencies" step. This scopes each engine's cache by OS and architecture (`macos15-x86_64`, `macos26-arm64`) via the `os-e2e-deps` action's existing `cache-scope` input, matching the pattern the Linux engines already use.

Also raises the macOS 15 `build` job timeout from 90 to 180 minutes. The Intel runner is the slowest builder in the fleet, and a cold sccache can push a from-scratch compile past the 90 minutes that suffices for the faster arm64/Linux runners, the same headroom already granted to windows-2025. Addresses #18359.

Both cache-scope changes were verified green on macOS 15 and macOS 26 via a temporary push-triggered validation workflow, removed before merge.
